brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Two-cell unit with tool bins and drawers. It's staged with a pen, a paint brush, a marker, a pencil and a 2 mm hex driver standing in the bin compartments.
Bottom storey: piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0. Top storey: piece:0,0,1 and piece:1,0,1 (all north-half bases).
A 2-compartment bin (bin:0,0,1, full-depth) and a 3-compartment bin (bin:1,0,1, full-depth) sit in the top storey.
drawer:0#0,0#cut is in the bottom storey. I also put a second drawer (drawer:0#1,0#cut) in the other bottom cell so its cut face isn't left open, so there are two drawers rather than one.
capOpenFaces added 10 solid end caps to every open face, and check_build reports no open faces. lockJoints was also run to bolt the joints.

finish.summary: I built a workbench organiser that is two cells wide and two storeys tall, using north-half bases. The bottom storey has a drawer in the cut face of each base, and the top storey holds a 2-compartment bin and a 3-compartment bin. Every open face is closed with solid end caps (10 caps), and all the joints are bolted. That comes to 34 parts. To show what it's for, I put a pen, a paint brush, a marker, a pencil and a 2 mm hex driver standing up in the bins. The configurator check passed with no rule issues, no prop warnings, and the parts don't collide.

M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
